assessment_goal: Identify and correct the off-by-one error that causes the algorithm to miss the last common character when scanning strings for LCP.
misconception_target: Assuming the loop terminates correctly when encountering a mismatch, ignoring the need to check the last character.

assessment_goal: Optimize the string scanning loop to reduce time complexity from O(n*m) to O(n) by using early exit and minimal comparisons.
misconception_target: Believing that scanning each string fully for each character is necessary.

assessment_goal: Explain how Java's memory model affects visibility of the LCP result in a multi-threaded environment.
misconception_target: Assuming that local variables are automatically thread-safe without synchronization.

assessment_goal: Refactor the LCP algorithm to use a divide-and-conquer approach and analyze its impact on time and space complexity.
misconception_target: Thinking that recursion always increases time complexity.

assessment_goal: Demonstrate how to apply memoization to avoid redundant comparisons in the LCP algorithm.
misconception_target: Assuming memoization is only useful for dynamic programming problems.
